_comments: MJ: Actions — three read-only cache projections over ActionEngineBase's caches. These replace
the memoized Params/ResultCodes/Libraries getters that MJActionEntityExtended used to hand-write:
cache + lazy + (default) read-only reproduces exactly what those getters did, generically.
These rows are LOAD-BEARING: ActionEngine, base-agent and MJActionEntityServer all consume
action.Params.Items / action.ResultCodes.Items from the GENERATED classes, and the hand-written
getters were deleted when these collections shipped. An environment whose EntityRelationship
rows lack these configs regenerates entity_subclasses.ts without the properties and the
workspace stops compiling — which is why every collection the code depends on must be seeded
here, not only in a developer database.

_comments: MJ: AI Agents — three collections, one writable and two read-only cache projections.
Prompts: the one related entity no engine caches, so it is database-sourced and writable.
AgentID is NOT NULL and ExecutionOrder is genuinely positional (which prompt runs first), so
it gets the Sequence policy. From is 0 because the column defaults to 0, not 1. Source and
ReadOnly are spelled out explicitly so the generated declaration is self-documenting next to
its cache-sourced siblings.
Actions: a read-only lazy view over BaseAIEngine's agent-action cache — this replaced both
MJAIAgentEntityExtended's hand-written getter and BaseAIEngine's manual association loop.
SubAgents: also a read-only lazy cache view (the ParentID hierarchy, ordered by
ExecutionOrder). Read-only means Add/Remove throw, so no OnRemove policy applies — nobody can
detach a sub-agent through this collection, which is the safe default for a self-referential
hierarchy where a careless 'delete' would destroy a whole agent. No Sequence policy either:
renumbering ExecutionOrder would rewrite the agent records themselves.
NOTE: MJ: AI Agents has a SECOND self-relationship (DefaultCoAgentID) which is deliberately
NOT declared — hence RelatedEntityJoinField in every lookup below, which is what keeps these
two rows apart.

_comments: MJ: AI Prompts -> MJ: AI Prompt Models. A read-only lazy view over BaseAIEngine's prompt-model
cache — zero queries on read, matching how prompt models are actually consumed.
Deliberately NO Sequence policy despite Priority being an integer: Priority is a SEMANTIC
ranking (which model to prefer), not a positional line number — and the collection is
read-only besides. OrderBy alone gives the read ordering without touching the values.

primaryKey.ID: @lookup:MJ: Entity Relationships.EntityID=@lookup:MJ: Entities.Name=MJ: AI Prompts&RelatedEntityID=@lookup:MJ: Entities.Name=MJ: AI Prompt Models&RelatedEntityJoinField=PromptID

_comments: MJ: API Keys -> MJ: API Key Scopes. A read-only lazy view over the APIKeyEngine cache.
Priority is a ranking, so no Sequence policy (same reasoning as AI Prompt Models above).
NOTE: because this collection is read-only, companion validation deliberately skips it — a
projection contributes no save work, so it contributes no validation either, and validating
would mutate the engine's shared instances via foreign-key stamping. Scope row-filter checks
(MJAPIKeyScopeEntityServer.ValidateAsync) therefore run when a scope record itself is saved,
not as a side effect of saving its API Key.
